overview: A broader version of the 16S question — any targeted marker approach versus reading the whole community's genetic material.
genZNote: Same sample, very different reading list.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Sequences a specific PCR-amplified marker region (e.g. 16S rRNA for bacteria, ITS for fungi) shared across a group of organisms.
aspects.valueB: Sequences total community DNA without any targeted amplification step, capturing all organisms and genes present.

aspects.label: Input Requirement
aspects.valueA: Requires only enough DNA for PCR amplification of the target marker; works well even with low-biomass or degraded samples.
aspects.valueB: Requires higher-quality, higher-quantity DNA input for representative whole-genome coverage.

aspects.label: Resolution and Bias
aspects.valueA: Resolution and detected diversity depend heavily on primer choice and PCR amplification bias.
aspects.valueB: Broader, less biased detection of community members, but sensitive to host DNA or contaminant background.

aspects.label: Computational Demand
aspects.valueA: Lower — established pipelines cluster or assign amplicon sequence variants relatively quickly.
aspects.valueB: Much higher — requires assembly, binning, and annotation across enormous, complex datasets.

aspects.label: Discovery Potential
aspects.valueA: Limited to organisms whose marker gene is captured by the chosen primers.
aspects.valueB: Can reveal genes, pathways, and organisms with no prior targeted marker, including novel or unculturable taxa.

aspects.label: Cost per Sample
aspects.valueA: Generally cheaper, enabling larger sample sizes for a given budget.
aspects.valueB: More expensive per sample, often limiting cohort size for a given budget.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Targeted marker gene, cheaper, primer-dependent bias.
aspects.valueB: Untargeted whole-community DNA, more expensive, broader discovery power.
